For most RVs, I'd pick by how you camp. The search results gave me only one direct buy link (marked below). For the others I've linked the review that covers them, so check current prices at the brand store or Amazon.

## Recommendations

**1. Full-timers, boondocking, or running the roof A/C: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous and 8,000 W surge
- Expandable past 12 kWh
- About 50 minutes to 80% from a wall outlet
- Under 30 dBA at light load, so it's fine during quiet hours
- It's the closest thing to a 30A campsite pedestal in battery form. One battery runs a 13,500 BTU A/C for about 2.3 hours, or a fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink for about 2 days.
- Downsides: it's a two-person lift and the priciest option once you add expansion batteries.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**2. Most capacity per dollar: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, 3,600 W at 120V, with an RV outlet
- Up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs (650 W max per input)
- 5-year warranty
- **$1,499, or $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12** (12% off orders over $1,200, expires Nov 15, 2026, tested in the store's cart Oct 23)
- **Buy:** [ALLPOWERS R4000 via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission.
- Caveats:
  - It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it suits a permanent spot in the RV, not carrying around.
  - The "4,000 W" in the title is the 230V rating.
  - ALLPOWERS' refund page says sale items can't be returned.
- Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

**3. Simplest A/C-capable setup: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- 3,024 Wh, 3,000 W continuous and 6,000 W surge, enough to start a 13,500 BTU A/C without a soft-start kit
- About $2,799
- Jackery is rated best for customer support.
- Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [OutdoorPowerStations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)

**4. Mid-range value with a 30A RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, 1,200 W solar input, about 62 lb
- Get this rather than the older AC200P, which some guides still list. The AC200P caps solar at 700 W, takes 5–6 hours to charge from the wall, and has only a 2-year warranty.
- Sources: [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [OutdoorPowerStations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)

**5. Weekend trips with no A/C: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, about 28 lb
- 1,000 W solar input, the highest in its class, and expandable to 5 kWh
- Source: [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Pairing solar panels

- **Match panels to the station's solar input limit.** Panels beyond the limit add nothing. For example, the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and 2000 v2 top out at 400 W.
- **Use separate inputs to reach the full rating.** The R4000 needs panels on all three inputs to hit 2,000 W. The DELTA 3 Plus needs two inputs to hit 1,000 W.
- **Size the array to the battery.** A 300–400 W folding array refills a mid-size (about 2 kWh) unit in a full day of good sun. A 3–4 kWh unit needs roughly 800 W or more for a daily refill.
- **Panel options:** The guides mention the brand's own folding panels (Jackery SolarSaga 100/200 W, EcoFlow folding or rigid panels) and the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase. I didn't get direct buy links for these. Brand-matched panels avoid connector and voltage mismatches.
- **Connecting to the RV:** A TT-30 "dogbone" adapter lets the station's 30A outlet feed your shore-power inlet. Get a licensed electrician for any hardwired transfer switch.

## Quick pick

| Your RV use | Pick |
|---|---|
| Running A/C off-grid, full-time | DELTA Pro 3 |
| Big capacity on a budget, mounted in place | ALLPOWERS R4000 |
| Weekends, fridge and devices only | DELTA 3 Plus or BLUETTI AC200L |

Note that every source here earns affiliate commissions. If you tell me your RV type, whether you need A/C, and your budget, I can narrow this to one combo with a specific panel count.
